Slice 5.1: fault-safe user copy + real SYS_DIAGCTL

The safety and observability floor every remaining Phase 5 slice stands
on. Grants (5.2), CDEV/TTY (5.3), VFS (5.4), MFS (5.8) and grant-sourced
exec (5.9) all move user bytes, and all of them need servers that can
speak while that machinery is still half-built.

D5 -- fault-safe user copy. The kernel no longer dereferences a user VA
anywhere, not even the active TTBR0's. New kernel/src/mm/uaccess.rs
page-chunks every range, resolves each page through the new
addrspace::walk_pt_in(ttbr0_pa, va) -> Option<(u64, Prot)> (the missing
member of the map_page_in / unmap_page_in / walk_leaves free-function
family; AddrSpace::walk_pt now delegates to it), and memcpys through the
frame's HHDM alias. An in-range-but-unmapped pointer was previously an
EL1 data abort with no fixup path -- a kernel panic. It is now EFAULT.

Because the walk is address-space-independent, no exception-fixup table
is needed (D5 rejected the Linux extable approach), and the deferred
MF_DELIVERMSG flush can write a receiver's buffer without that receiver's
TTBR0 being installed -- so sched::schedule_next's TTBR0-before-flush
ordering stops being load-bearing; only eret still needs it.

Two properties the old write_volatile got for free and this does not:
copy_to_user_as must check Prot::writable, because the HHDM alias is a
kernel mapping the MMU's EL0 permission bits do not police; and writes
are all-or-nothing (probe_user_range first), because a 104-byte Message
is only 8-aligned and really can straddle two pages, so copy-as-you-go
would leave a half-written message behind on failure.

Error routing: EFAULT reaches the caller's x0 through do_ipc for the
three immediate sites (mini_send, kernel-call request, kernel-call
reply), and a blocked receiver's *parked* x0 for the deferred flush --
p.regs.x[0] = e as i64 as u64, the MINIX retreg idiom
do_exit::unblock_dependents already uses -- replacing a `let _ =` that
dropped the error. That path also sets and clears MF_MSGFAILED, which
has existed unused since Phase 2.

ipc/message.rs ends with zero unsafe: messages stage through a [u8; 104]
and are reassembled by infallible indexing, so every raw-pointer
operation in the user-copy path is in mm::uaccess alone. offset_of!
asserts tie its M_TYPE_OFF / PAYLOAD_OFF to the real Message layout --
without them a field added ahead of payload would be a silent miscopy,
since the slice length would still be correct.

The page-split arithmetic (page_chunks / PageChunk / USER_PAGE_SIZE) is
in kernel-shared beside user_va_ok, because the kernel crate has no
#[cfg(test)] and this is the one piece with real off-by-one risk.
kernel-shared goes 60 -> 68 tests. Granule coupling that was previously
convention is now pinned: USER_PAGE_SIZE == FRAME_SIZE in uaccess.rs
(chunker and walker live in different crates), FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE
and 1 << PAGE_SHIFT == PAGE_SIZE in addrspace.rs.

D2 -- SYS_DIAGCTL. Servers run at EL0 with no console; every bring-up bug
so far has been diagnosed indirectly through kernel traces. The call
takes a MINIX-numbered subcode (DIAGCTL_CODE_DIAG = 1, 2-4 reserved and
EINVAL) and carries its text *inline* in the payload -- length in 4..8,
up to DIAG_TEXT_MAX = 88 bytes from DIAG_TEXT_OFF = 8. Inline rather than
MINIX 3's (buf, len) user pointer precisely so the debug channel needs no
user-copy machinery and cannot fault: it has to work while the copy
engine and grants are themselves under construction.

The [diag <name>] prefix is the caller's kernel-known Proc::name, never
payload data, so a server can only identify itself -- the anti-spoof
property DS already relies on for m_source. Text is sanitized to
printable ASCII, which is what guarantees one call is exactly one line
and keeps the grep -aF marker contract intact. No new privilege wiring:
k_call_mask already restricts kernel calls to server-grade privs and the
shared USER priv has an empty mask.

server-rt::diag_print is the client, chunking longer strings. It is
called from sef_startup (before init_fresh, so the line proves
SYS_DIAGCTL independently of DS), so all six SEF servers announce
themselves for one line of code.

Proof. Four one-shot probes on stub A's prologue cover every arm of the
engine: an unmapped page, a page-straddling buffer (8 bytes in A's stack
page, 96 in the unmapped page above), the deferred-flush path, and a
mapped-but-read-only destination for the writable check. The last was
added on review -- without it a regression dropping that check would
still have passed every marker; it is mutation-tested, stubbing the check
out makes exactly that marker disappear. A fifth stub was rejected:
NR_STUB_PROCS feeds FORK_POOL_BASE, so it would shift init's forked
children 15 -> 16 and break three existing markers.

Boot markers go 26 -> 31, all unsampled so they cannot drift with IPC
ordering (the [ipc N] form embeds a running counter). qemu-boot.forbidden
gains the same-EL banner "!!! kernel exception (vector index", the sharp
canary for exactly the regression this slice prevents.

The highest risk here was *surfacing* a previously-silent failure: the
kernel-originated notifies (deliver_alarm, deliver_ksig, mini_pf_send,
send_no_quantum) set MF_DELIVERMSG on a proc whose deliver_msg_vir came
from its own last RECEIVE, and the old `let _ =` swallowed a bad one. The
guard is a stub-free boot grepped for [efault], which must be empty. It
is, across both feature configurations.

Drive-bys, per the slice scope and slice 5.0's nominations:
NR_KERN_CALLS_PHASE4 -> NR_KERN_CALLS (25 references; the C header always
emitted the un-suffixed name and the two must not diverge past the 5.6
ABI freeze -- a test now forbids any phase-scoped name in the header);
sef.receive(..) != 0 -> != OK, which was 5 sites, not the 9 slice 5.0
estimated, since drivers/, fs/ and userland/ have no receive loops yet;
ipc_const.rs's trap-ABI comment said x16 where the register is x1; and
the stale slice-2.5-era module docs in ipc/{message,senda,mod}.rs plus
arch/aarch64/userland.rs, which still promised this slice's own work as
future slice-3.4 work.
